editorial:
Imagine being a man of God who cannot stop thinking about things that are strictly forbidden. You get to meet Father Miguel, a priest who is completely torn apart by his own desires. He tries to do the right thing by asking his church superiors for help, but they basically ignore him or tell him to just deal with it. It creates this heavy, tense feeling where you can tell he is reaching a breaking point. The movie feels like a peek into a secret world where faith and human nature clash in a way that feels very real and uncomfortable.

What really works here is how the acting makes you feel sorry for Miguel even when he makes bad choices. The pacing is steady, though it might feel a bit slow if you are looking for a big thriller. If you like stories about secret lives and moral struggles, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you should look for a high-quality version to really see the details. I suggest adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best experience, or you can try renting it on Apple TV if you just want a quick watch.
endingExplained: In the end, Miguel cannot fight his urges anymore and gives in to his temptations. He finds himself trapped in a cycle of guilt and shame that he cannot escape. The movie wraps up by showing that the church's refusal to help him actually pushed him further away from his faith. He ends up broken and alone, proving that ignoring a person's mental struggle only makes the situation much worse in the long run.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty character studies and stories about forbidden desires.
